_meta._note: All values are now sourced from log files in results/. Any value without a confirmed log is marked as 'unverified' in the corresponding field. Earlier _note fields claiming 'NOT re-run yet' are now resolved or downgraded to honest 'unverified' markers.

_multiseed._note: 3-seed pilot 2026-06-12. NAC gain over TTC is +2.79pp (std 0.34), consistent with paper's single-seed 2.99pp claim.

table2_multi_eps.description: 5 datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, Flowers-102, ImageNet-100). DTD excluded due to low absolute robust accuracy at eps=4 introducing disproportionate variance.

table3_nstep._source: All K=2 and K=4 values verified 2026-06-12 (small PGD random-init noise: ~0.4-0.9pp).
table3_nstep.description: PGD eps=4/255, K=2,4, seed=0. All verified.

eps_symmetric_control.description: CRITICAL CONTROL: defense budget matched to attack budget. Reveals that NAC's gain is partly a budget-asymmetry artifact at low eps.

configs._note: NAC loses by 3.01pp under fair budget
NAC wins by 8.22pp under fair budget
NAC wins by 9.81pp under fair budget

eps_symmetric_control.key_finding: NAC's reported +2.99pp at eps_att=1/255 (Table 2) DISAPPEARS under matched-budget control: TTC actually wins by 3.01pp at eps=1. NAC's advantage is real only at moderate-to-high attack strengths (eps >= 2/255). This requires qualifying the paper's main claim.

optimizer_comparison.description: Adam optimizer for counterattack (CIFAR-10, PGD eps=4/255, K=2, seed 0). NAC's Nesterov look-ahead vs Adam.
optimizer_comparison.key_finding: NAC (16.47) > Adam (5.38) by +11.09pp and > TTC (7.07) by +9.40pp. Adam is the WORST optimizer tested, supporting the paper's claim that Nesterov look-ahead is specifically effective (not just 'any optimizer').

table5_cross_model._RN50_note: Verified 2026-06-12: both TTC and NAC give ~0% on RN50. NAC achieves a marginal 0.01pp (essentially zero), confirming the paper's claim that NAC is not effective on RN50's attention-pooled embedding space. RN50 is sensitive to pixel-space perturbations beyond ViT-tuned hyperparameters' capacity.

super_additive.interpretation: 0.85 + 1.64 = 2.49 << 9.40 (NAC gain). This super-additive result remains the central claim.

momentum_ablation.description: CIFAR-10, PGD eps=4/255, 10 attack steps, K=2, seed=0. tau_thres=0.2, beta=2.0.

tau_beta_sensitivity._source: results/tau_beta/nac_tau*_seed0.json (CIFAR-10, PGD eps=4/255, K=2, NAC m=0.9, seed=0). Note: defended values differ ~0.7pp from the main NAC=16.47 result due to PGD random-init across separate runs.
tau_beta_sensitivity.description: CIFAR-10, PGD eps=4/255, K=2, seed=0. Varies tau_thres (default 0.2) and beta (default 2.0).

configs._note: tau too small -> gating too strict
beta too small -> soft weighting less discriminative

tau_beta_sensitivity.takeaway: NAC is robust to hyperparameter choice around (tau=0.2, beta=2.0). tau=0.1 halves accuracy; beta=1.0 reduces by 4pp; beta=3.0 gives marginal +1.3pp improvement.

config_B_K4_alpha3.description: DOC paper default: K=4, step_size=3/255, seed=0
config_B_K4_alpha3._honest_observation: At Config B (K=4, alpha=3/255) in seed=0, DOC (40.38%) actually OUTPERFORMS NAC (38.33%) by +2.05pp. This contradicts the earlier draft claim of NAC > DOC. We have removed that claim and now report this finding honestly.
